newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: UN envoy reports progress in Congo peace talks.
newsitem.headline: UN envoy reports progress in Congo peace talks.

text.p: Talks on ending a two-month-old conflict in Congo have made progress, a United Nations mediator said on Sunday, but he warned against excessive optimism in a dispute that has left hundreds dead in the West African state.

"I can confirm that both sides have now agreed on a government of national unity, and that a new prime minister will be chosen on the basis of consensus," UN special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun told BBC radio.
He also said President Pascal Lissouba could be staying on after his mandate expired at the end of August, until an election orginally planned for July 27 could be rescheduled.
Sahnoun stressed that the negotiations were continuing. "This is only part of an argument resolved," he said.
The dispute has pitted forces loyal to Lissouba against the militia of his predecessor, Denis Sassou Nguesso.
Lissouba had been opposed to a consensus prime minister, while Sassou was against Lissouba staying on after August.
Sahnoun has been holding peace talks with representatives of both men in Libreville, the capital of Gabon.

He made a brief trip to Brazzaville on Friday in an attempt to break the deadlock by talking directly to Lissouba and Sassou, as well as to Bernard Kolelas, the mayor of Brazzaville, whose own militia have stayed out of this latest fighting.
"I went to Brazzaville where I had talks with President Lissouba, General Sassou, Mayor Kolelas, Prime Minister (Charles) Ganao and some other political leaders," Sahnoun told Reuters on Saturday.

"I was able to go over the whole issue and I tried to do the necessary to speed up the Libreville talks, for the longer we hang around, the greater the chances the situation on the ground will deterioriate," he said.
He said that the Libreville talks would resume on Monday.
The crisis blew up on June 5, when Lissouba's troops surrounded Sassou's residence with armoured vehicles as part of a crackdown on private militia.
The fighting has left hundreds dead and tens of thousands displaced. Whole districts of the capital Brazzaville have been devastated.
A fragile truce is holding in Brazzaville, which was reported calm this weekend.
